newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed on thin volume ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed on thin volume ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed mixed on thin volumes as investors remained largely sidelined ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) interest rate policy meeting on Tuesday, dealers and analysts said.
"People are not buying or selling. They are all waiting for the outcome of the FOMC meeting," said a TA Securities dealer.
An analyst said the market was expecting a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates, but added that "an increase of more than 25 basis points would have some negative impact here".
The Composite Index of 100 large capitalised shares closed up 1.66 points at 1,214.60.
The all-share EMAS index ended 0.50 lower at 354.78 and the Second Board index was up 0.71 to 664.51.
Dealers said they expected the market to rebound after the FOMC meeting, following two weeks of consolidation.
"I believe those who wanted to sell have sold over the last two weeks," said one dealer with a local firm.

The stock of property and manufacturing firm Selangor Dredging was again the most active counter with 22.7 million shares traded. It closed one cent lower at 2.56 ringgit after earlier rising to a 12-month high of 2.70. Dealers said a local stockbroking firm was a heavy buyer of the shares.
